name: Voltaire
biography: Identified as the principal transmitter of Locke's (and later Hume's) influence into eighteenth-century France, via his Lettres philosophiques. Rousseau's great rival and correspondent; quoted mocking the Discourse on Inequality ('One longs, in reading your book, to walk on all fours') and disputing with Rousseau over the Lisbon earthquake and the morality of theatre.
